sanskrit: adhyardhayojanaṃ gatvā nadīṃ paścān mukhāśritām sarayūṃ puṇyasalilāṃ dadarśa raghunandanaḥ
english: Having travelled a yojana and a half, the delight of the Raghu line beheld the river whose waters are sacred — the Sarayū, flowing toward the west.

sanskrit: atha tasmin muhūrte tu brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ sarvaiḥ parivṛto devair ṛṣibhiś ca mahātmabhiḥ
english: At that very moment Brahmā, the grandfather of all worlds, surrounded by all the gods and by great-souled sages,

sanskrit: āyayau yatra kākutsthaḥ svargāya samupasthitaḥ vimānaśatakoṭībhir divyābhir abhisaṃvṛtaḥ
english: came to the place where Kākutstha stood ready to ascend to heaven — attended by hundreds of millions of divine celestial chariots.

sanskrit: papāta puṣpavṛṣṭiś ca vāyumuktā mahaughavat
english: A great torrential shower of flowers fell, released by the wind like a vast flood.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tūryaśatākīrṇe gandharvāpsarasaṃkule sarayūsalilaṃ rāmaḥ padbhyāṃ samupacakrame
english: While hundreds of instruments resounded and the place was thronged with Gandharvas and Apsarases, Rāma stepped on foot into the waters of the Sarayū.

sanskrit: tataḥ pitāmaho vāṇīm antarikṣād abhāṣata āgaccha viṣṇo bhadraṃ te diṣṭyā prāpto 'si rāghava
english: Then the grandfather spoke from the sky: "Come, O Viṣṇu — may good befall you! By good fortune have you arrived, O Rāghava."

sanskrit: bhrātṛbhiḥ saha devābhaiḥ praviśasva svakāṃ tanum vaiṣṇavīṃ tāṃ mahātejas tad ākāśaṃ sanātanam
english: "Together with your brothers who are equal to gods, O great-radiant one, enter your own form — that eternal Vaiṣṇava body and that everlasting sky."

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi lokagatir deva na tvāṃ ke cit prajānate ṛte māyāṃ viśālākṣa tava pūrvaparigrahām
english: "For you, O lord, are the refuge of all worlds. None know you truly, O wide-eyed one, except through that primal Māyā which you previously assumed."

sanskrit: tvam acintyaṃ mahad bhūtam akṣayaṃ sarvasaṃgraham yām icchasi mahātejas tāṃ tanuṃ praviśa svayam
english: "You are the inconceivable great being, imperishable, the totality of all. O greatly radiant one, of your own will enter whatever form you desire."

sanskrit: pitāmahavacaḥ śrutvā viniścitya mahāmatiḥ viveśa vaiṣṇavaṃ tejaḥ saśarīraḥ sahānujaḥ
english: Having heard the grandfather's words and having resolved upon it, the great-minded one, together with his brothers and still in his bodily form, merged into the radiance of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: tato viṣṇugataṃ devaṃ pūjayanti sma devatāḥ sādhyā marudgaṇāś caiva sendrāḥ sāgnipurogamāḥ
english: Then the gods worshipped the divine one who had entered Viṣṇu — the Sādhyas, the host of Maruts, Indra and the others, with Agni at their head.

sanskrit: ye ca divyā ṛṣigaṇā gandharvāpsarasaś ca yāḥ suparṇanāgayakṣāś ca daityadānavarākṣasāḥ
english: The divine companies of sages, the Gandharvas and Apsarases, Garuḍas, Nāgas, Yakṣas, and the Daityas, Dānavas and Rākṣasas —

sanskrit: sarvaṃ hṛṣṭaṃ pramuditaṃ sarvaṃ pūrṇamanoratham sādhu sādhv iti tat sarvaṃ tridivaṃ gatakalmaṣam
english: — all were rejoicing, all were delighted, all had their heart's desire fulfilled. "Well done! Well done!" cried all of them, free of sin, as they rose to the triple heaven.

sanskrit: atha viṣṇur mahātejāḥ pitāmaham uvāca ha eṣāṃ lokāñ janaughānāṃ dātum arhasi suvrata
english: Then Viṣṇu, of great splendour, spoke to the grandfather: "O faithful one, you should grant worlds to these multitudes of people."

sanskrit: ime hi sarve snehān mām anuyātā manasvinaḥ bhaktā bhājayitavyāś ca tyaktātmānaś ca matkṛte
english: "For all these noble ones have followed me out of love; they are devoted and deserve a fitting reward, having surrendered themselves for my sake."

sanskrit: tac chrutvā viṣṇuvacanaṃ brahmā lokaguruḥ prabhuḥ lokān sāntānikān nāma yāsyantīme samāgatāḥ
english: Hearing the words of Viṣṇu, Brahmā, the lord and preceptor of all worlds, declared: "These assembled ones shall go to the worlds called Sāntānika."

sanskrit: yac ca tiryaggataṃ kiṃ cid rāmam evānucintayat prāṇāṃs tyakṣyati bhaktyā vai saṃtāne tu nivatsyati sarvair eva guṇair yukte brahmalokād anantare
english: "And whatever being, even among the lower creatures, meditating on Rāma alone, shall give up its life in devotion — it shall dwell in the offspring, endowed with all virtues, in the realm next to Brahmaloka."

sanskrit: vānarāś ca svakāṃ yonim ṛkṣāś caiva tathā yayuḥ
english: The Vānaras and the bears likewise returned to their own respective origins.

sanskrit: yebhyo viniḥsṛtā ye ye surādibhyaḥ susaṃbhavāḥ ṛṣibhyo nāgayakṣebhyas tāṃs tān eva prapedire
english: Those who had been born from gods and others, from sages, Nāgas and Yakṣas — each returned to those very origins from which they had come forth.

sanskrit: tathoktavati deveśe gopratāram upāgatāḥ bhejire sarayūṃ sarve harṣapūrṇāśruviklavāḥ
english: When the lord of gods had spoken thus, all of them came to the ford called Gopratāra and entered the Sarayū, their eyes swimming with tears of joy.

sanskrit: avagāhya jalaṃ yo yaḥ prāṇī hy āsīt prahṛṣṭavat mānuṣaṃ deham utsṛjya vimānaṃ so 'dhyarohata
english: Every living being that plunged into the waters, filled with great delight, cast off its human body and ascended a celestial chariot.

sanskrit: tiryagyonigatāś cāpi saṃprāptāḥ sarayūjalam divyā divyena vapuṣā devā dīptā ivābhavan
english: Even those born in lower wombs, upon reaching the waters of the Sarayū, became divine; with celestial forms they shone like gods ablaze with light.

sanskrit: gatvā tu sarayūtoyaṃ sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca prāpya tat toyavikledaṃ devalokam upāgaman
english: The stationary and the mobile — all, upon reaching the waters of the Sarayū and being immersed in that sacred flood, attained the world of the gods.

sanskrit: devānāṃ yasya yā yonir vānarā ṛṣkarākṣasāḥ tām eva viviśuḥ sarve dehān nikṣipya cāmbhasi
english: Whatever divine origin the Vānaras, bears and Rākṣasas had — each one of them entered back into that very origin, having cast off their bodies in the waters.

sanskrit: tathā svargagataṃ sarvaṃ kṛtvā lokagurur divam jagāma tridaśaiḥ sārdhaṃ hṛṣṭair hṛṣṭo mahāmatiḥ
english: Having thus sent all to heaven, the great-minded preceptor of the worlds, himself rejoicing, departed to the sky together with the rejoicing gods.

sanskrit: etāvad eva ākhyānaṃ sottaraṃ brahmapūjitam rāmāyaṇam iti khyātaṃ mukhyaṃ vālmīkinā kṛtam
english: This alone is the narrative, together with the Uttara-kāṇḍa, honoured by Brahmā, known as the Rāmāyaṇa — the foremost work composed by Vālmīki.
